description: Machine-readable source of truth for the EngineOS router. 32 entries for CLAUDE.md's 31 '| Intent (signals) | Load |' table rows — the +1 is the mobile store-release row split into ios-release/android-release intents — which stays the human mirror. scripts/validate-engineos.sh checks this file: C16 against CLAUDE.md (row count, drift alarm) and against registries/routing.json (every hook_mirrored intent carries a domain FK whose rules array matches the registry), and resolves every unqualified rule, skill and agent name to a file under rules/, skills/ and agents/; C18d checks suppression data integrity; C19 checks required_sections/required_fields/archive_contract (handoff, P4); C21 checks the record-change archive contract (P6). Plugin-qualified skill names (superpowers:*) and the external code-review skill are not resolved locally. v2 (2.0.0, contracts.md@rev2 §1.2) adds the scoring fields of the Tier 1 classifier (src/kernel/score.ts) beside every kept signals array: phrases (weighted; every signal stays a phrase at weight 1 or more (agent-system multi-agent and orchestration signals at 1.5), except migration at 0.3 in big-sweep and backend because dba owns it, plus phrases calibrated by T13d at 0.3-1.5, evidence in evals/BASELINE.md), verb_object (a verb + object pair counted once; calibrated weight 0.4-0.5 so a pair alone stays below policy.json router.scoring.min_score while a pair plus the top exemplar similarity can route), negative (subtracted phrases), exemplars (3-10 BM25 documents per active intent, C38b), threshold (the judge cut for intent.<id>, greater than 0 and at most 1; placeholders until the judge shadow calibration recorded in evals/BASELINE.md) and router_row, the CLAUDE.md table cells that src/gen/router-table.ts renders between the engineos:router-table markers (C38d). Rows are in table order; android-release carries no router_row because the generator folds it into ios-release's store-release row. C38 checks the v2 shape.

intents.title: New feature / multi-file change
intents.note: New behavior with no more-specific row below; a more specific matching row suppresses this one. The from-scratch flow runs through the new-feature command: PRD + ADR + SPEC + TASKS before code, then whichever stack rows also match — so this row names no rules of its own. EXTERNAL skill: tlc-spec-lean is pinned from tech-leads-club/agent-skills in skills-lock.json and installed unchanged, not shipped under skills/; Matt Pocock's grill-with-docs, to-spec and to-tickets are human-invoked (disable-model-invocation) and run through the command, so they are not listed here. The flow applies at non-negotiable #1's threshold (>2 files or any new feature); a small single-file tweak skips straight to the stack rules. Once tasks exist, always-on rules/parallelism.md dispatches independent tasks as parallel agents. model_tier is null because the tier is delegated to the command's stages and to the matched stack rows. Acceptance criteria precede code. Test/check implementation and execution are deferred until all code is integrated and the user explicitly approves current-task final tests; an external skill cannot authorize earlier tests.
exemplars: add a csv export button to the invoices page
implement password reset by email for user accounts
build a notifications inbox where users see unread alerts
create a wishlist so customers can save items for later
let admins invite teammates to a workspace with a role

router_row.intent: New feature / multi-file change ("add", "build", "create", "implement") — new behavior with no more-specific row below; a more specific matching row suppresses this one
router_row.load: `/engineos:new-feature` — PRD + ADR + SPEC + TASKS before code: Matt Pocock skills `grill-with-docs` (ADRs → `docs/adr/`, glossary `CONTEXT.md`) → `to-spec` (PRD → `docs/prds/`) → skill `tlc-spec-lean` plan and acceptance criteria, then implementation (SPEC → `.specs/features/<feature>/`, indexed from `docs/specs/`) → `to-tickets` (TASKS → `docs/specs/<feature>/tickets/`, each naming the acceptance criteria it closes) → parallel build and integration → final non-test validation → test authoring/execution only with explicit current-task user approval; then stack rules below. Applies at non-negotiable #1's threshold — a small single-file tweak skips straight to the stack rules. Once tasks exist, apply `rules/parallelism.md`: independent tasks dispatch concurrently within min(policy cap, available host slots), refilling completed slots as dependencies become ready

intents.title: Big / multi-domain / sweep work
intents.note: Both named rules are already always-on; the row names them to make the fan-out obligation explicit. Fan out via /engineos:implement <domain> <task> for changes, /engineos:audit for analysis, or N Task calls in ONE message over disjoint scopes. /engineos:implement dispatch is spec-gated. Tier is design: the row's primary work is fan-out planning and task decomposition, not the changes themselves.
exemplars: update every service to the new logging format across all packages
backfill the created_by column for all existing orders
rename the tenant id field in every module and every test
move all repositories from the old http client to fetch
apply the new error envelope across every module in the monorepo

router_row.intent: Big / multi-domain / sweep work (>3 files, >1 domain, ≥3 independent tasks, "across all X", migration, backfill)
router_row.load: Apply `rules/parallelism.md` + `rules/models.md` from the task contract; fan out — `/engineos:implement <domain> <task>` for changes, `/engineos:audit` for analysis, or N Task calls in ONE message over disjoint scopes. Skills: `superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents`, `superpowers:subagent-driven-development`; `/engineos:implement` dispatch is spec-gated

intents.title: Work complete / close the change record

archive_contract.note: The change record is where delivered work claims conformance with its spec: spec: names the design-doc that rule-spec-threshold required, ## Verification carries the output-shown that rule-verification required, and the record itself is rule-change-record's artifact. Template checked by C21b, archived instances by C21c/C21d, prose mirrors by C21e. domains is deliberately NOT an FK to routing.json.domains — that enum routes file paths to hook domains (and has ios-release/android-release, no docs/general); this one files completed work. Records completed before grandfathered_before predate the schema and are never checked (archived/README.md: not migrated). instance_sections_since carries the P6 cutoff: the three evidence sections became scaffolded and required on 2026-08-06; earlier archived records legitimately lack them and the archive is read-only except for factual errors.

intents.title: Ambiguous or multi-agent request needing a dispatch plan
intents.note: The router agent runs one scripts/kernel.sh resolve call FIRST and reasons only about the residue: intent tiebreaks the notes do not settle mechanically, scope decomposition against real files, and wave grouping. It returns a dispatch plan; it never dispatches and never edits. Tier is design per registries/models.json work type architecture, which covers task decomposition and fan-out planning. The deterministic path needs no agent at all — hooks/prompt-advisor.sh emits the kernel's answer directly when route-escalate reports escalate=false.
exemplars: route this request and tell me which agents should do it
who should do this, it touches the api, the app and the database
give me a dispatch plan for this work without starting it

intents.title: Claiming done / complete / fixed; spec archived / feature shipped
intents.note: Evidence before assertion, always. For spec-archive and ship cases: lint, typecheck, build and an API/Web startup check, output shown, with a bounded fix loop — attempts, escalation and the never-repair floors per registries/policy.json repair, answered per attempt by scripts/kernel.sh repair; exhausting the bound reports red, never done. The Stop hooks stop-verify.sh and record-verify.sh are the automated half — they gate on scoped lint/typecheck and on an unrecorded change record; approved final tests run separately after integration — and they cover the Validation gate only, never the Release gate.
exemplars: the spec is done, move it to the archive
show evidence that the feature is complete before calling it done
verify the fix actually works before we say it is fixed
we are archiving this spec, run the final gate first
